tags.qa_notes: Deep re-audit 2026-09-25 (6 sources re-fetched live). All previously confirmed facts hold: 144ft island cargo freighter (reconfirmed by mystkittsdivebuddy.com, padi.com, dive-the-world.com), Hurricane Hugo split her into two sections ~50ft apart in 1989 (reconfirmed by every source checked), resting on sand/seagrass off Frigate Bay with a sunken van/minibus and bulldozer nearby amid Port Zante construction rubble (reconfirmed). Sinking-year conflict persists unresolved by design: 1981 (mystkittsdivebuddy.com, divenevis.com, padi.com, prodiversstkitts.com - prodiversstkitts.com additionally specifies 'near Fort Tyson' and frames it as 'sunk in 1981 hurricane') vs 1985 (dtmag.com, reconfirmed this pass). NEW ANOMALY FOUND: padi.com's own dive-site page currently states 'Maximum Depth 12 feet / 3 meters', which conflicts with the 12m/40ft depth given by the other 5 sources and appears to be a unit-entry error on PADI's site (not used; depth kept at 12m). padi.com also lists 'sharks, whales, and dolphins' for this site - unsupported by any of the other 5 sources and implausible for a shallow 12m harbor-adjacent wreck; treated as a generic regional-sightings widget rather than a site-specific claim and excluded from the description. Tonnage and build date: still undocumented in any source, including a fresh scubago.com fetch which had no site-specific content - correctly left unstated rather than invented. Marine life reconfirmed: turtles, eels, octopus, porcupine fish, stingrays (multi-source); mystkittsdivebuddy.com's wreck page also credits 'resident barracuda (historically)', added with that caveat. No Wikipedia article exists for this vessel (reconfirmed).

Re-audit 2026-09-25 (4 sources re-fetched live). Nurse sharks, moray eels, and large spiny lobsters at deep overhangs, and the flying gurnard, all reconfirmed across mystkittsdivebuddy.com ('The Monkeys'), prodiversstkitts.com, activecaribbeantravel.com, and dtmag.com. DEPTH CONFLICT CLARIFIED: mystkittsdivebuddy.com and prodiversstkitts.com both independently give 40-70ft (12-21m), while only activecaribbeantravel.com gives a deeper 40-100+ft (12-31m) range - the majority of sources cap depth near 21m. Kept depth=31m (the outlier's upper bound, conservative for divers) but the conflict is now stated explicitly in the markdown rather than left implicit. Added prodiversstkitts.com as a 4th independently-fetched confirming domain. No hallucinations found on this pass.

Re-audit 2026-09-25. Re-confirmed via fresh fetch: activecaribbeantravel.com still describes this wreck as under 25ft (8m), beginner/reef-fish, novice-friendly - no new detail. A fresh direct fetch of mystkittsdivebuddy.com's wreck-diving-sites page (which lists Corinthian, River Taw, Talata, and Liamuiga) again confirms Brassball is not present. Fresh fetches of both of prodiversstkitts.com's current site-list pages (/pages/sites.html and /st-kitts-dive-sites/) also confirm no mention of Brassball. WebSearch across ScubaBoard and Scuba Diving Magazine (scubadiving.com, blocked by HTTP 403) found nothing further. STATUS DOWNGRADED validated true -> false per the 3-source-minimum deep-QA standard: only 1 independently verifiable domain exists for this site. The prior 2026-07-03 pass identified this exact 1-source shortfall in its own notes but left the validated flag at 'true'; this pass corrects that inconsistency. No vessel history (name origin, build date, tonnage, sinking cause) has ever been found for this wreck - correctly left undocumented rather than invented.

Re-audit 2026-09-25. frommers.com content reconfirmed via WebSearch cache (site still returns HTTP 403 to direct fetch/curl and to WebFetch) with the same figures: ~3km/2mi west of Four Seasons Nevis, max depth 21m, Atlantic spadefish and large sea fans. No second or third independent source could be found despite fresh searches - PADI's own 'Coral Garden' dive-site pages found in general search results are for Oman and South Africa, not St Kitts/Nevis; dive-the-world.com, padi.com, both of prodiversstkitts.com's current site-list pages, and ScubaBoard were all checked and contain nothing for this site. STATUS DOWNGRADED validated true -> false per the 3-source-minimum deep-QA standard: only 1 domain, and that domain cannot even be directly verified (search-index synthesis only, not a direct fetch). The prior pass flagged this exact issue in its own notes ('flagged as unresolved, the weakest-sourced site in this destination') but left validated at 'true'; this pass corrects that inconsistency.

Re-audit 2026-09-25. activecaribbeantravel.com reconfirmed via fresh fetch: Atlantic side of St Kitts, 50-80ft (15-24m), 'diverse marine life' with no species named. A fresh WebSearch targeted specifically at ScubaBoard for 'Grid Iron St Kitts' returned no results referencing this site. Fresh direct fetches of mystkittsdivebuddy.com's reef-diving page and both of prodiversstkitts.com's current site-list pages confirm none of them mention Grid Iron. STATUS DOWNGRADED validated true -> false per the 3-source-minimum deep-QA standard: only 1 verifiable domain. The prior pass's own notes already flagged this shortfall but left validated at 'true'; corrected here. Per marine-life-accuracy rule, markdown continues to state that regional fauna is expected but names no species.

Re-audit 2026-09-25 (5 sources re-fetched live). Anchors-field claim reconfirmed again: dtmag.com and dive-the-world.com both independently describe colonial-era anchors embedded in the reef/seabed. CORRECTION TO PRIOR AUDIT: the 2026-07-03 notes described Pro Divers as reporting a shallow 12-18m 'Sandy Reef', but a fresh direct fetch of prodiversstkitts.com's current site list instead gives 'Sandy Point Reef' at 50-130ft (15-40m) - matching Active Caribbean Travel and Dive Training Magazine's deeper range, not the shallow one. Only mystkittsdivebuddy.com now gives a shallower 40-60ft (12-18m) figure for a site of the same name (close to shore, deep canyons/swim-throughs, variable visibility). Depth conflict restated accordingly: 3 sources (Pro Divers, Active Caribbean Travel, Dive Training Magazine) support the deeper 15-40m range; 1 source (My St Kitts Dive Buddy) supports a shallower 12-18m figure. Kept depth=40m, matching the majority. MARINE LIFE CORRECTION: mystkittsdivebuddy.com separately lists a 'Paradise Reef' entry (one of the two mooring areas that make up this combined site) naming barracuda, turtles, nurse sharks, moray eels, rays, and conch - nurse sharks and moray eels are therefore now confirmed for this site's Paradise Reef component, correcting the prior pass's statement that 'no source confirms nurse sharks... at this specific site.' dive-the-world.com's 'Anchors Aweigh' entry additionally and independently confirms frogfish and pike blennies among the anchors, and its separate 'Paradise Reef' entry confirms pike blennies alongside turtles/lobsters/barracuda/angelfish - added to the marine life list.

Re-audit 2026-09-25 (4 sources re-fetched live, see correction below). Drift-dive/Advanced classification reconfirmed independently again by activecaribbeantravel.com ('for experienced divers only') and dtmag.com ('St. Kitts' only drift dive... for experienced divers'). Volcanic mini-wall, fire coral, sea urchins, and eagle rays feeding in nearby grass beds reconfirmed via a fresh direct fetch of prodiversstkitts.com's current site list. Nag's Head North details (southern stingrays, tarpon, brown chromis) reconfirmed via a fresh direct fetch of divenevis.com's current dive-sites page. SOURCE CORRECTION: a fresh direct fetch of mystkittsdivebuddy.com's current 'reef diving sites of St Kitts' page shows a 12-site list (The Rock, South Brimstone, Bird Rock Reef, Camps Reef, Challengers Reef, Finger Reef, Friars Bay Reef, Harbor Reef, The Monkeys, The Vents, Paradise Reef, Sandy Point Reef) that does NOT include Nag's Head at all. The prior 2026-07-03 pass credited mystkittsdivebuddy.com for the eagle-ray/grass-bed detail; that detail is genuinely confirmed, but by prodiversstkitts.com, not mystkittsdivebuddy.com. mystkittsdivebuddy.com has been removed from this site's validation_source and markdown footer as an unverified citation for Nag's Head specifically. Still 4 verified domains, above the 3-source minimum. No hallucinations found beyond the already-removed reef-shark/pelagic/hawksbill claims from the prior pass.

Re-audit 2026-09-25 (3 sources re-fetched live). All claims reconfirmed without change: reef/wall from ~12m to ~31m (Active Caribbean Travel), sand grottos (Pro Divers, listed there as 'Coconut Tree Rocks'), grunts/snapper/groupers/barracuda/spotted moray/lobsters/rays (Dive The World, Pro Divers), nurse sharks (Active Caribbean Travel, Dive The World). No new information, no conflicts found, no hallucinations found. Difficulty (Intermediate) and depth (31m) unchanged.

Re-audit 2026-09-25. Both existing sources reconfirmed: Frommer's (via WebSearch cache; site still returns HTTP 403 to direct fetch) still gives south tip of Nevis, ~20-minute boat ride from Four Seasons, coral grottoes, squirrelfish/turtles/needlefish, suitable for certified and resort divers. Active Caribbean Travel reconfirmed directly (listed there as 'Devil's Caverns'): several swim-throughs, max depth 40ft (12m), corals and sea fans. A fresh ScubaBoard search and fresh direct fetches of divenevis.com and both of prodiversstkitts.com's current site-list pages found no additional mention of this site. STATUS DOWNGRADED validated true -> false per the 3-source-minimum deep-QA standard: only 2 domains, one of which (Frommer's) cannot be directly verified. The prior pass flagged this same shortfall in its own notes but left validated at 'true'; this pass corrects that inconsistency.

Re-audit 2026-09-25. divenevis.com reconfirmed via a fresh direct fetch of its current /dive-sites/ page: 'Booby High Shoals', near Booby Island in the Narrows, circular reef, lobster, French grunts, horse-eye jacks, southern stingrays, hawksbill turtles, nurse sharks up to 10-12ft sheltering under ledges - all details hold. caribdiveguide.com could not be reached directly this round either (DNS resolution fails for this connection, same as before) but its cached content, re-surfaced via WebSearch, is unchanged: flat terrain of old coral heads 3-5ft high, overhangs, circular reef with lobster/stingrays/grunts/horse-eye jacks/hawksbill turtles at Booby Island - still treated as a lower-confidence, search-index-only citation pending a direct fetch. Wikipedia's 'Booby Island' article reconfirmed as geographic corroboration only (no dive-site content), still counted as the 3rd distinct domain per the prior pass's reasoning. No hallucinations found; no changes to depth, difficulty, or site type.
